reason: The passage portrays the elite—particularly King Josiah and his officials (the high priest Hilkiah, scribe Shaphan, and other court officials)—in decidedly favorable terms. Josiah is explicitly described as doing 'that which was right in the eyes of the Lord' (וַיַּעַשׂ הַיָּשָׁר בְּעֵינֵי יְהוָה), walking in the way of his father David without deviation, and demonstrating a tender heart that humbled itself before God. The officials are portrayed as faithful, competent, and righteous in executing the king's commands for religious reform. Even the prophetess Huldah, a figure of authority and wisdom, is treated respectfully. The negative elements in the text concern idolatry and false worship practices (which the elite actively work to eliminate), not the character of the elite themselves.
